# Vocabulary-driven phrases

The vocabulary functions are authoritative; the product is always recomputed. `extended` adds teal only at the source, reusing the original colors. Strings denote words, with `""` denoting an empty alternative. No macro or asserted operation types are needed.

```shen
(define v-check
  {string --> boolean --> boolean}
  _ true -> true
  Label false -> (simple-error Label))

(define v-colors
  {symbol --> (list string)}
  original -> ["amber" "violet"]
  extended -> (append (v-colors original) ["teal"])
  _ -> (simple-error "unknown vocabulary version"))

(define v-objects
  {--> (list string)}
  -> ["kite" "cup"])

(define v-join
  {string --> string --> string}
  "" Y -> Y
  X "" -> X
  X Y -> (@s X " " Y))

(define v-row
  {string --> (list string) --> (list string)}
  _ [] -> []
  X [Y | Ys] -> [(v-join X Y) | (v-row X Ys)])

(define v-product
  {(list string) --> (list string) --> (list string)}
  [] _ -> []
  [X | Xs] Ys -> (append (v-row X Ys) (v-product Xs Ys)))

(define v-phrases
  {symbol --> (list string)}
  Version -> (v-product (v-colors Version) (v-objects)))

(define v-unique?
  {(list A) --> boolean}
  [] -> true
  [X | Xs] -> (and (not (element? X Xs)) (v-unique? Xs)))

(v-check "original four in source order"
  (= (v-phrases original)
     ["amber kite" "amber cup" "violet kite" "violet cup"]))
(v-check "extended six from changed source"
  (= (v-phrases extended)
     ["amber kite" "amber cup" "violet kite" "violet cup" "teal kite" "teal cup"]))
(v-check "original has no duplicates" (v-unique? (v-phrases original)))
(v-check "extended has no duplicates" (v-unique? (v-phrases extended)))
(v-check "empty alternatives on either side have no padding"
  (= (v-product ["" "amber"] ["" "cup"])
     ["" "cup" "amber" "amber cup"]))
(v-check "no alternatives is not epsilon" (= (v-product [] ["cup"]) []))
```

For finite lists, `v-row` visits each object once; `v-product` visits each color once and concatenates exactly those rows. This proves completeness of the Cartesian product by structural induction. With distinct source words and unambiguous single-word nonempty colors/objects, rendering is injective, so each phrase occurs once. Arbitrary multiword or duplicate/empty sources could render distinct choices identically; the generator intentionally preserves such multiplicity rather than silently deduplicating it. Epsilon is an alternative, whereas an empty list offers no alternatives. Types establish string-list shape, not this completeness or uniqueness argument. No user declarations or untyped boundaries.

# Structurally indexed persistent history

Newest is the head of an immutable list; appending chronologically therefore constructs a new head. Index `0` is empty and `[succ N]` is nonempty. These are concrete representation rules, not axioms asserting operation results. Double-line rules allow decomposition, so all operation bodies below are checked.

```shen
(datatype h-history
  _________________________
  [] : (h-history A 0);

  X : A; P : (h-history A N);
  =======================================
  [X | P] : (h-history A [succ N]);)

(define h-empty
  {--> (h-history A 0)}
  -> [])

(define h-append
  {A --> (h-history A N) --> (h-history A [succ N])}
  X P -> [X | P])

(define h-newest
  {(h-history A [succ N]) --> A}
  [X | _] -> X)

(define h-remove
  {(h-history A [succ N]) --> (h-history A N)}
  [_ | P] -> P)

(define h-double-newest
  {(h-history number [succ N]) --> (h-history number [succ N])}
  H -> (h-append (* 2 (h-newest H)) (h-remove H)))

(define h-check
  {string --> boolean --> boolean}
  _ true -> true
  Label false -> (simple-error Label))

(h-check "replacement, unchanged source and predecessor"
  (let P (h-append 7 (h-empty))
       H (h-append 11 P)
       Alias H
       R (h-double-newest H)
    (and (= (h-newest R) 22)
      (and (= (h-remove R) P)
        (and (= (h-newest (h-remove R)) 7)
          (and (= (h-newest Alias) 11)
               (= (h-remove H) P)))))))
(h-check "single-item replacement retains empty predecessor"
  (= (h-remove (h-double-newest (h-append 3 (h-empty)))) (h-empty)))
(h-check "removal leaves old history usable"
  (let H (h-append 4 (h-empty))
       P (h-remove H)
    (and (= P (h-empty)) (= (h-newest H) 4))))
```


<!-- reject: h-read-removed-sole -->

The replacement consumes a successor-indexed input, removes one head, and reconstructs exactly one head. Its signature checks length preservation; the body specifically reuses the predecessor, which is also tested. List reductions give newest(append(x,p)) = x and remove(append(x,p)) = p. No mutation is performed. These are implementation arguments, not consequences of arrow types alone. No untyped definitions or `declare`; trust remains in the concrete datatype theory, built-ins, and runtime. The datatype is open: adding inconsistent rules could invalidate rejection guarantees. Indices alone do not prove ordering, purity, termination, or arbitrary element immutability.

# Cyclic prerequisite closure

Use a typed explicit worklist rather than unrestricted recursive Prolog closure: finite graph traversal needs a visited set regardless of engine. The independent catalog includes isolated docs. Input must be a ground catalog symbol; an unknown symbol raises an error. Ordinary evaluated Shen calls supply values, not Prolog logic variables.

```shen
(define p-jobs
  {--> (list symbol)}
  -> [seed compile package publish docs])

(define p-direct
  {symbol --> (list symbol)}
  seed -> [package]
  compile -> [seed]
  package -> [compile]
  publish -> [package]
  docs -> []
  _ -> (simple-error "unknown job"))

(define p-walk
  {(list symbol) --> (list symbol) --> (list symbol) --> (list symbol)}
  [] _ Answer -> (reverse Answer)
  [J | Todo] Seen Answer -> (p-walk Todo Seen Answer)
    where (element? J Seen)
  [J | Todo] Seen Answer ->
    (p-walk (append (p-direct J) Todo) [J | Seen] [J | Answer]))

(define p-requirements
  {symbol --> (list symbol)}
  J -> (p-walk (p-direct J) [J] []) where (element? J (p-jobs))
  _ -> (simple-error "input must be a catalog job"))

(define p-unique?
  {(list symbol) --> boolean}
  [] -> true
  [X | Xs] -> (and (not (element? X Xs)) (p-unique? Xs)))

(define p-check
  {string --> boolean --> boolean}
  _ true -> true
  Label false -> (simple-error Label))

(p-check "publish closure" (= (p-requirements publish) [package compile seed]))
(p-check "cycle excludes starting seed" (= (p-requirements seed) [package compile]))
(p-check "isolated catalog job" (= (p-requirements docs) []))
(p-check "all catalog closures are unique and exclude their input"
  (every? (/. J (and (p-unique? (p-requirements J))
                    (not (element? J (p-requirements J)))))
          (p-jobs)))
```

`Seen` initially contains the input, so even a cycle cannot return it. Each newly visited vertex schedules all its outgoing prerequisites once. Every reachable non-input vertex is eventually processed: skipping a seen vertex loses no successors because they were already scheduled, except for the root whose successors were scheduled initially. Only five vertices can expand; each expansion adds a finite list and each iteration removes a work item. Thus traversal terminates and the accumulated answer contains each reachable non-input job once, in first-visit order.

The tests assert exact ordered lists, not just counts. `not` is Boolean negation of a ground membership test, not negation-as-failure on an unbound query. This is a closed finite graph; changes must keep all edge endpoints in the catalog. Signatures establish list/symbol shapes, not reachability correctness or catalog consistency. No declarations or untyped boundaries.

# Typed token parser and AST evaluator

Input is a flat token list, not source text. Numbers and symbols share a token type; only `plus` and `times` are recognized operators. The grammar constructs tagged AST nodes, not merely a trusted declared result. Tails are semantic functions accumulating on the left; product parsing is nested inside sum parsing.

```shen
(datatype e-token
  N : number;
  ____________
  N : e-token;

  S : symbol;
  ____________
  S : e-token;)

(datatype e-ast
  N : number;
  ==================
  [literal N] : e-ast;

  L : e-ast; R : e-ast;
  ====================
  [sum L R] : e-ast;

  L : e-ast; R : e-ast;
  ====================
  [product L R] : e-ast;)

(datatype e-number-guard
  ______________________________________
  (number? X) : verified >> X : number;)

(datatype e-branch-evidence
  Test : boolean; Test : verified >> X : A; (not Test) : verified >> Y : A;
  _____________________________________________________________________
  (if Test X Y) : A;)

(defcc <e-expression>
  {(list e-token) ==> e-ast}
  <e-term> <e-sums> := (<e-sums> <e-term>);)

(defcc <e-sums>
  {(list e-token) ==> (e-ast --> e-ast)}
  plus <e-term> <e-sums> := (/. Left (<e-sums> [sum Left <e-term>]));
  <e> := (/. Left Left);)

(defcc <e-term>
  {(list e-token) ==> e-ast}
  <e-number> <e-products> := (<e-products> <e-number>);)

(defcc <e-products>
  {(list e-token) ==> (e-ast --> e-ast)}
  times <e-number> <e-products> :=
    (/. Left (<e-products> [product Left <e-number>]));
  <e> := (/. Left Left);)

(defcc <e-number>
  {(list e-token) ==> e-ast}
  N := [literal N] where (number? N);)

(define e-evaluate
  {e-ast --> number}
  [literal N] -> N
  [sum L R] -> (+ (e-evaluate L) (e-evaluate R))
  [product L R] -> (* (e-evaluate L) (e-evaluate R)))

(define e-parse
  {(list e-token) --> e-ast}
  Tokens -> (compile (fn <e-expression>) Tokens))

(define e-fails?
  {(list e-token) --> boolean}
  Tokens -> (trap-error (do (e-parse Tokens) false) (/. E true)))

(define e-check
  {string --> boolean --> boolean}
  _ true -> true
  Label false -> (simple-error Label))

(e-check "precedence AST"
  (= (e-parse [2 plus 3 times 4])
     [sum [literal 2] [product [literal 3] [literal 4]]]))
(e-check "precedence evaluation" (= (e-evaluate (e-parse [2 plus 3 times 4])) 14))
(e-check "repeated plus left AST"
  (= (e-parse [1 plus 2 plus 3])
     [sum [sum [literal 1] [literal 2]] [literal 3]]))
(e-check "repeated times left AST"
  (= (e-parse [2 times 3 times 4])
     [product [product [literal 2] [literal 3]] [literal 4]]))
(e-check "repeated mixed evaluation"
  (= (e-evaluate (e-parse [1 plus 2 times 3 times 4 plus 5])) 30))
(e-check "empty rejected" (e-fails? []))
(e-check "missing operand rejected" (e-fails? [2 plus]))
(e-check "adjacent operators rejected" (e-fails? [2 times plus 3]))
(e-check "leading operator rejected" (e-fails? [plus 2]))
(e-check "trailing number rejected" (e-fails? [2 plus 3 4]))
(e-check "trailing unknown symbol rejected" (e-fails? [2 plus 3 unknown]))
```

A malformed semantic action is rejected by the typechecker:

<!-- reject: <e-bad-action> -->
```shen
(defcc <e-bad-action>
  {(list e-token) ==> e-ast}
  N := [sum [literal 1]];)
```

`compile` requires complete consumption; the trailing-input assertions exercise that contract. There is no left recursion: each recursive tail alternative consumes an operator and an operand before recursion, while epsilon does not recurse. Thus the grammar terminates on finite input under the runtime's grammar semantics. Operator alternatives precede epsilon. AST equality, rather than arithmetic alone, distinguishes left from right associativity (addition/multiplication would hide the difference).

Trusted logical bridges: the `number?` verified rule assumes the built-in predicate really recognizes numbers; the conditional rule exposes facts valid in the selected branch. They are not parse-result declarations. Grammar semantic actions and evaluation bodies are checked under these rules. No untyped boundary or `declare` is used. Types alone do not prove exact language recognition, consumption, precedence, termination, purity, numeric precision, or correctness of a future lexer. Error tests recognize any parse-time exception, not a particular diagnostic; tests are finite evidence, not an exhaustive parser proof.

# Immutable policy, explicit account state

A configuration captures only a nonnegative debit fee. Each call supplies the current balance and an action. A successful result contains the new balance; insufficient funds is an explicit alternative, not a mutated balance or an exception. Negative configuration, balance, or amount is invalid and raises an error. Tests use exact small integers; arrow types admit numbers more broadly.

```shen
(datatype a-action
  N : number;
  =====================
  [credit N] : a-action;

  N : number;
  ====================
  [debit N] : a-action;)

(datatype a-result
  N : number;
  ==========================
  [balance N] : a-result;

  ______________________________
  insufficient-funds : a-result;)

(define a-credit
  {number --> number --> a-result}
  Balance Amount -> [balance (+ Balance Amount)]
    where (and (>= Balance 0) (>= Amount 0))
  _ _ -> (simple-error "negative balance or credit"))

(define a-debit
  {number --> number --> number --> a-result}
  Fee Balance Amount ->
    (if (>= Balance (+ Amount Fee))
        [balance (- Balance (+ Amount Fee))]
        insufficient-funds)
    where (and (>= Balance 0) (>= Amount 0))
  _ _ _ -> (simple-error "negative balance or debit"))

(define a-step
  {number --> number --> a-action --> a-result}
  _ Balance [credit Amount] -> (a-credit Balance Amount)
  Fee Balance [debit Amount] -> (a-debit Fee Balance Amount))

(define a-configure
  {number --> (number --> a-action --> a-result)}
  Fee -> (a-step Fee) where (>= Fee 0)
  _ -> (simple-error "negative debit fee"))

(define a-check
  {string --> boolean --> boolean}
  _ true -> true
  Label false -> (simple-error Label))

(a-check "independent fee configurations and replay"
  (let Low (a-configure 1)
       High (a-configure 4)
    (= [(Low 20 [debit 5]) (High 20 [debit 5]) (Low 20 [debit 5])]
       [[balance 14] [balance 11] [balance 14]])))
(a-check "credit does not pay debit fee"
  (= ((a-configure 4) 20 [credit 5]) [balance 25]))
(a-check "predecessor remains unchanged and reusable"
  (let Before 20
       Step (a-configure 1)
       After (Step Before [debit 5])
    (and (= Before 20)
      (and (= After [balance 14]) (= (Step Before [credit 2]) [balance 22])))))
(a-check "overdraft includes fee"
  (= ((a-configure 2) 10 [debit 9]) insufficient-funds))
(a-check "exact funds allowed"
  (= ((a-configure 2) 10 [debit 8]) [balance 0]))
(a-check "failed transition has no hidden state"
  (let Step (a-configure 2)
       Failure (Step 10 [debit 99])
    (and (= Failure insufficient-funds) (= (Step 10 [debit 8]) [balance 0]))))
```

## Separately: genuinely private mutation

The counter's cell is allocated once per factory call and is never returned. Aliases of a returned closure share it. These counters are independent of account transitions.

```shen
(define a-counter-command
  {(vector number) --> symbol --> number}
  Cell peek -> (<-vector Cell 1)
  Cell tick -> (let Next (+ 1 (<-vector Cell 1))
                   Write (vector-> Cell 1 Next)
                Next)
  _ _ -> (simple-error "unknown counter command"))

(define a-counter
  {number --> (symbol --> number)}
  Start -> (let Cell (vector 1)
               Init (vector-> Cell 1 Start)
             (a-counter-command Cell)))

(a-check "aliases share, factories do not"
  (let C (a-counter 0)
       Alias C
       Other (a-counter 0)
       One (C tick)
       Shared (Alias peek)
       Two (Alias tick)
    (= [One Shared Two (C peek) (Other peek) (Other tick) (C peek)]
       [1 1 2 2 0 1 2])))
```

All bodies are checked, without declarations or untyped boundaries. The action/result rules specify concrete shapes. They do not encode nonnegative amounts, conservation, replay, isolation, purity, ownership, or any invocation protocol. Configuration isolation and replay follow by inspecting the account body: only captured numeric Fee, explicit inputs and arithmetic are used. Counter sharing/freshness instead depends on allocation and vector mutation semantics, supported by assertions. Runtime arithmetic, immutable numeric values, evaluation order and stable built-ins remain assumptions. The fee is fixed per returned closure, not a claim that arbitrary captured objects are immutable. No serialization, concurrency or general effect proof is supplied.

# Review: client checking is not implementation checking

The claim is false. The operation rules are trusted axioms over untyped closure code. A client proof uses the asserted type of `push`, without inspecting its body. Changing that body to return the original stack leaves the axioms and hence client proofs unchanged.

## Smallest counterexample (proposed, not executed)

Let `e = empty`, and consider `s = push(1, e)`. The asserted rules assign `s : stack number [succ 0]`, so `top(s)` typechecks. The actual push returns `e`; it has not added an item. Thus the claimed length change and law `top(push(1,e)) = 1` are unsupported. The precise runtime symptom of `top(e)` depends on the empty closure implementation; it might error or return some other value. No execution result is claimed here.

A second distinguishing observation, if a nonempty baseline can be constructed independently, is pushing a different value and testing that top changes. Do not rely on the broken push to create that baseline.

## Smallest repair and evidence strategy

1. Fix push to construct a fresh node/closure retaining both the new element and the old stack. Review the dispatch reductions for `top(push(x,s)) = x` and `pop(push(x,s)) = s`. Closure code left untyped still requires a reviewed correspondence to its asserted interface.
2. Prefer a concrete persistent representation with checked constructors and destructors: empty list at index 0 and cons at successor index, with introduction **and elimination** rules. Check the actual bodies. A proposed push claiming a successor while returning its input should then be a named negative implementation test, not merely a rejected client.
3. Enable checking before loading implementations. Test the two equations, an empty/singleton boundary, multiple distinct values, predecessor observations and old aliases after updates. Require type errors for reading empty and reading after removing the sole item. Assertions must error on mismatch. These are proposed checks, not invented outcomes.
4. If closure representation is retained, explicitly list untyped definitions, asserted operation judgments, and the relation between a closure and the abstract sequence it represents. Establish empty correspondence, push preservation and observation agreement. Differential tests against a checked list representation provide supporting evidence, not universal equivalence.

## What each layer establishes

- **Client checking under axioms:** legal compositions relative to those axioms and the active, extensible datatype theory. It does not validate the axioms or implementation.
- **Checked concrete bodies:** representation/index obligations of each normally returning result. The checker still depends on sound concrete rules and the runtime; it does not supply every semantic law automatically.
- **Length indices:** structural size/nonemptiness only, under the representation assumptions. Two equal-length stacks can have different elements or orders. Even replacing top with the wrong value can preserve the length type.
- **Ordering and predecessor preservation:** require content laws and body reasoning, with tests as finite evidence.
- **Persistence and purity:** require absence of destructive interference and effects, or an explicit justified ownership/effect discipline. Hidden mutation can invalidate an alias's old index. Persistent structure does not imply deeply immutable elements.
- **Termination:** requires a decreasing structural argument or other termination evidence; ordinary arrow types permit divergence and exceptions.

For this review no code is executed and no test result is asserted. The runtime checker does not turn this prose into a proof. The repair must be checked and exercised on the actual library before claiming implementation correctness.

# Trial report

## Result

Completed all six self-contained task files under `answers/`. The required checker reported **10 blocks, 0 failed (shen-jit)**: six accepted fences and four expected type-error fences. Accepted fences include runtime assertions that raise errors on mismatch. Review is intentionally prose-only and has no executable fence.

- `BIFROST_SHEN_JIT=/private/tmp/bifrost-skills-drive/jit-v05/shen-jit-0.5-macos-arm64/shen-jit`
